quizzes.stem: An extraction schema marks the purchase order number as required, and invoices lacking one come back with believable numbers that appear nowhere in the documents. What fixes it?

options.a: Add a minimum length so that short numbers are refused
options.b: Allow a null for that field when the source gives none
options.c: Tell the model never to leave a required field empty
options.d: Set a default of `unknown` in the schema for that field

explanation.b: A field that may be missing from the source is nullable, so that the model is not pushed to fabricate a value.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a length limit "would not tell a real number from an invented one".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a required field pushes the model to fabricate a value", and the instruction adds to the pressure.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a default that looks like data is a problem because "downstream code cannot tell it from a real value".

quizzes.stem: A strict schema is in force, and one record lists line items that add up to 120.50 beside a total of 130.00. Which statement holds?

options.a: A type check catches it, because a total is just a number in the record
options.b: Strict mode catches it as soon as the tool definition sets `strict`
options.c: Required fields must agree with each other, so the validator rejects it
options.d: Nothing in the contract catches it: shape is promised, meaning is not

explanation.d: The guide says strict schemas do not prevent semantic errors, and a sum is one.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A strict schema makes the first kind rare and does nothing about the second", and both numbers pass a type check.
explanation.b: Ruled out because strict schemas "do not prevent semantic errors", and this record already matches its shape.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "the guarantee is about shape", which covers presence of fields and not agreement between them.

quizzes.stem: An extraction fails a check because the printed total differs from the sum of the lines, and the record has `conflict_detected` set to true. What should the pipeline do?

options.a: Retry with the error message appended to the prompt
options.b: Replace the printed total with the computed one
options.c: Route it to a person with the discrepancy noted
options.d: Mark the document failed once the retry limit is reached

explanation.c: A flagged conflict is information about a bad source, and a second look finds the same difference.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a second look will find the same difference", so the retry cannot change the outcome.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A record that carries a difference and says so is a correct record of a bad document", and replacing the printed value hides what it says.
explanation.d: Ruled out because this record is not invalid, since "a document that is still invalid after the last one is marked failed" applies to errors that are retried.

quizzes.stem: A pipeline reports 98 percent accuracy over the documents that passed its checks, while 30 percent of all documents did not pass. What is wrong with the figure?

options.a: It leaves out the failures, so it flatters the system
options.b: It is too low, because a passed document is always correct
options.c: It counts each document twice, once per validation rule
options.d: It is right, since only passed documents have a verdict

explanation.a: The denominator is filtered by the pipeline's own verdict, which drops the documents most likely to be wrong.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the report "divides by the documents that passed", so it overstates and does not understate.
explanation.c: Ruled out because it "leaves out the documents that went to review or failed", and nothing is counted twice.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The first number is true and answers a different question".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A 300-page contract is cut into chunks, and the per-chunk results are merged. Two chunks give different vendor names. Which merge rule fits?

options.a: Take the later value, since it was read with more context
options.b: Keep the first value, note the clash and send it to a person
options.c: Take the longer name, since it carries more detail
options.d: Drop the field from the merged result to avoid a wrong value

explanation.b: A disagreement between chunks is a conflict to record and review, and not a choice to make silently.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A merge that always takes the last value or the longest is a guess presented as data".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a later chunk with a different vendor is to be handled with "do not pick silently", and choosing the longer name is the same kind of pick.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the rule is to record the clash "so that the document goes to review", and dropping the field hides it.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A team extracts invoice fields. Each failed extraction gets two more attempts. One failure is a currency written outside the allowed list, and another is a purchase order number that the document does not contain but downstream needs. Which handling is right?

options.a: Send the first back with its error, and route the second to review untried
options.b: Send both back with their errors until each field has a value
options.c: Send neither back and mark both documents failed at once
options.d: Route the first to review and send the second back with a stricter, firmer prompt

explanation.a: The currency error is fixable by a second look and the missing number is absent from the source.
explanation.b: Ruled out because for an absent value "No second look will find what is not there".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a format error is what feedback is for, since "The information is in the document; the form was wrong".
explanation.d: Ruled out because it inverts the two, while "A required value that the model reports as absent is not retried".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A team extracts invoice fields with a strict schema through a forced tool, and caches a long instruction block and a 200-page document. For some requests it switches `tool_choice` from `any` to `auto` and back, and costs run above plan. What explains it?

options.a: Each change also discards the stored tool definitions and the system prompt text
options.b: Moving between modes turns off structured output for the next request
options.c: Each change discards stored conversation content, which is processed again
options.d: Requests in automatic mode are billed at a higher rate than the others

explanation.c: Changing the mode invalidates cached message blocks, so the content must be reprocessed.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Tool definitions and system prompts remain cached".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the documented effect of a change is on the cache: "changing tool_choice between requests invalidates cached message blocks".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the cost described is reprocessing, since a pipeline that alternates modes "pays to reprocess the document".
